title: Kofi and the Almost-Perfect Machine
subtitle: A Copper Tree story to colour and create
audience: Ages 5–8, independently or shared with an adult

pages.heading: A muddle of pencils
pages.text: On rainy afternoons, six friends squeezed into the Lookout, their clubhouse in Copper Tree Garden. Today, Amara needed a green pencil. She found three red ones, a sock and a biscuit crumb. Kofi pushed his round glasses up his nose. “We need a pencil machine.” “Does it draw?” asked Eli. “Does it make biscuits?” asked Tayo. “It sorts,” said Kofi.
pages.activity: Design a pencil pot for the Lookout. Add a picture that helps everyone recognise it.
pages.art_brief: Kofi beside clubhouse table with a broad shallow tray of pencils, Amara searching; room for a large empty pencil-pot outline.

pages.heading: The secret project
pages.text: At Uncle Deji’s repair workshop, Kofi drew a ramp with three little doors. You chose a door, and your pencil slid into its pot. Uncle Deji helped prepare smooth cardboard pieces and watched Kofi fit them together. “Who will try it?” he asked. “Everyone. When it’s perfect.” Kofi covered his plan with his sleeve. He wanted their first look to be a wonderful one.
pages.activity: Draw three different signs for the machine’s three doors. They can be shapes, colours or pictures.
pages.art_brief: Kofi and friendly Black adult Uncle Deji at safe clear workshop table, cardboard ramp and three wide doors; no cutting tools in child hands.

pages.heading: Almost
pages.text: Kofi tried a short pencil. It slid into a pot. He tried a long pencil. It stuck sideways. He tried two pencils. They met in the middle and refused to move. “Traffic jam,” said Uncle Deji. Kofi moved a door and tried again. This time a pencil rolled onto his shoe. His machine was almost perfect. Unfortunately, almost was taking ages.
pages.activity: Invent a funny name for this machine. Draw the name or a symbol on its sign.
pages.art_brief: Kofi looking down at a pencil on his shoe, small cardboard sorting ramp on tabletop, blank large sign area.

pages.heading: Under the cloth
pages.text: On Saturday, Kofi carried the machine to the Lookout with Uncle Deji. A cloth hid its three pots. His friends crowded round. “Can we see?” asked Zuri. “It needs one tiny change,” said Kofi. He bent over the ramp. A pot tipped. Pencils pattered across the table. Kofi pulled the cloth over everything. “Perhaps we should do something else.”
pages.activity: Draw what a friend could say when somebody’s plan goes wrong.
pages.art_brief: Kofi embarrassed beside cloth-covered table, a few fallen pencils, Zuri nearby with gentle concerned expression; open speech bubble.

pages.heading: A small question
pages.text: Eli stopped reaching for a pencil. “Do you want help picking them up?” Kofi nodded. Nobody called the machine silly. Nobody went away. Uncle Deji sat beside him. “Which part would you like us to look at?” Kofi rubbed the cloth between his fingers. Then he lifted one corner. “The pencils keep getting stuck. I thought you might laugh.”
pages.activity: Draw a friendly face and one way you could help Kofi feel welcome.
pages.art_brief: Eli collecting pencils from tabletop while Kofi lifts cloth, Uncle Deji seated beside him; supportive body language, no ridicule.

pages.heading: One pencil at a time
pages.text: “I’d like to try,” said Nia. Kofi passed her a pencil. She held it sideways above the ramp. “Which way does it go?” Kofi blinked. He had always pointed his pencils straight down. “That way,” he said. Amara drew an arrow. They tried again. The pencil slid neatly into a pot. Kofi let out a breath he had been holding.
pages.activity: Draw a big arrow on your own invention. What would it help somebody do?
pages.art_brief: Nia holding a pencil lengthwise at ramp entrance, Amara adding a bold arrow, Kofi watching with relief; large blank design box.

pages.heading: The stubborn pencil
pages.text: A longer pencil still caught at the bend. Zuri watched from the side. “It needs more room.” Uncle Deji helped Kofi widen the turn. Eli held the empty pot steady. Tayo crouched until his eyes were level with the ramp. “Mission control is ready.” Kofi released the pencil. It slid round the bend. “Landing successful!” whispered Tayo much too loudly.
pages.activity: Draw a path for a pencil to follow. Give it plenty of room around the bends.
pages.art_brief: Side view of broad cardboard ramp curving into pot, Kofi releasing pencil, Tayo watching at table height; open area for freehand route.

pages.heading: A useful mistake
pages.text: Then they tried a chunky crayon. It stopped at the entrance. Kofi frowned, but this time he left the cloth alone. “That opening is too narrow.” “Crayons could have their own tray,” said Eli. Nia tried reaching the farthest door. “And could this handle be closer?” Kofi fetched his notebook. Soon there were more ideas than blank spaces.
pages.activity: Design a special resting place for chunky crayons. Make its opening easy to reach.
pages.art_brief: Kofi taking notes with Eli suggesting broad crayon tray, Nia indicating far handle; chunky crayon visibly too wide for narrow original opening.

pages.heading: Everybody has a go
pages.text: They made the handles easier to reach and added a wide crayon tray. Amara decorated the pots with different shapes. Now nobody needed to remember which pot was which. Each friend tried the machine while Kofi watched. He wanted to reach in and help. Instead, he asked, “What happened?” Sometimes the answer was “It worked!” Sometimes it was “Look at this.”
pages.activity: Draw three pots, each with a different shape on the front. Colour them any way you like.
pages.art_brief: Three large pots marked circle triangle star, broad tray alongside, friends taking turns calmly; strong readable geometric symbols.

pages.heading: The grand opening
pages.text: On Sunday, Mrs Bennett visited the Lookout. Kofi stood beside his machine. His stomach felt full of jumping beans. “It sorts pencils,” he said. “You choose a door and send one down. The crayons go here.” Mrs Bennett tried a blue pencil. Plonk! It landed in the star pot. “Excellent,” she said. “Where do you put a muddy gardening glove?”
pages.activity: Draw an invention that would help Mrs Bennett in the garden. It can be wonderfully silly.
pages.art_brief: Kofi demonstrating tabletop sorter to Mrs Bennett in gardening clothes, glove held separately; friends laughing kindly, machine works.

pages.heading: The most important part
pages.text: “Definitely outside,” said Nia, and everyone laughed. Amara retrieved her green pencil from the pot she had chosen. Kofi watched her begin a picture. His machine had a crooked corner and a patch of tape showing. It also had six people’s ideas in it. “What’s it called?” asked Zuri. Kofi considered. “The Almost-Perfect Pencil Machine.” “Catchy,” said Eli. “Needs a bigger sign.”
pages.activity: Create the machine’s celebration sign. Add a symbol for everyone who helped.
pages.art_brief: Working sorter with visible tape patch, Amara drawing, Kofi proudly beside it; large blank banner for reader contribution.

pages.heading: The next idea
pages.text: They put Kofi’s first drawing on the Lookout’s discovery shelf. Beside it, he placed a fresh sheet. “I’ve got another idea,” he said. “It’s only a scribble.” Six heads leaned together. Tayo pointed at a round shape. “Biscuit maker?” “A place to keep everyone’s muddy boots,” said Kofi. Tayo sighed. “One day.” Kofi handed him a pencil. “What would you add?”
pages.activity: Draw your own almost-perfect idea. Add one thing a friend might suggest.
pages.art_brief: Six friends gathered around large blank sheet on clubhouse table; first ramp drawing on discovery shelf; warm joyful ending.

scenes.art_brief: Kofi at a tidy workshop table beside Uncle Deji, designing a simple cardboard pencil sorter with a wide ramp, three flap doors and three pots. Large clear shapes, paper plan on table, warm encouragement. Kofi wears round glasses and striped shirt. No power tools or blades.

Kofi at the Lookout table with cloth partly covering a small cardboard pencil sorting ramp. One pot has tipped and several pencils lie on the table. His expression is embarrassed, Zuri looks kindly concerned. Sparse clubhouse background.

Nia tries placing a pencil lengthwise at the start of the cardboard ramp while Amara draws a large arrow on the entrance and Kofi watches with relief. Three pots at ramp end, spacious table. Children retain reference hairstyles and clothes.

Kofi and Tayo observe one pencil travelling down a wide curved cardboard ramp towards a pot. Eli steadies pot. Beside ramp sits a chunky crayon and broad open tray suggesting their next improvement. Child-friendly simple mechanical shapes.

Kofi proudly demonstrates completed cardboard pencil sorter to Mrs Bennett, a warm older Black woman in gardening clothes. Three pots labelled only with circle triangle star symbols, and separate broad crayon tray. Mrs Bennett holds a muddy glove away from machine. No text.

Six Copper Tree friends happily lean around a broad table holding one large blank sheet for their next idea. Kofi offers Tayo a pencil. Finished pencil sorting ramp sits at side of table. Lookout discovery shelf in background holds an old tin and simple framed drawing. Large uncluttered colouring areas.
